title: Do brain training games actually work
titleChinese: 智力开发类游戏“效果甚微”
paragraphs: If you don't use it, you lose it. At least, that's how the old aphorism goes. It refers to the idea that something which does not get utilised regularly quickly falls into a state of decline. For example, a hobby that you haven't done for a few years, like playing the trumpet. You might find yourself a bit rusty the next time you pick one up - or maybe you've forgotten altogether! Muscles are another example. They will waste away without use. In order to counteract this, people take regular exercise to keep their skills sharp.

Well, what about the brain? As we age, our brains can naturally begin to decline. In some cases this can lead to certain mental conditions such as dementia, which I‘m sure you will agree, no one wants. However, all is not lost because these days it’s relatively easy to train your brain. Smartphones and apps have put programmes into our hands that can test, maintain and even augment our memories, mathematical skills, logic skills and a raft of other mental abilities. With a little practice every day, we can keep our brains nice and sharp, right?

Well, no, actually. According to a report from the Global Council on Brain Health, even though many people thought it was important to play online games, such as puzzles and mind games, which are designed to improve brain health, the evidence of the benefits was “weak to non-existent”. Playing a ‘brain game‘ may lead to improvements in game performance, but this has yet to show a convincing result in people’s daily cognitive abilities. In other words, doing hundreds of sudoku puzzles might make you a sudoku wizard, but it doesn‘t necessarily improve your ability to do your accounting.

It’s not all doom and gloom though. There are other ways to stimulate the old grey matter. It recommends seeking out new activities that challenge the way you think and are socially engaging, while leading to a healthy lifestyle. Among their suggestions are practising tai chi, taking photography classes, learning new technologies, gardening, art projects or volunteering.

There‘s more good news, too. James Goodwin, chief scientist at Age UK has said that brain decline is not inevitable. As long as the activities are “new to you and require your concentrated attention”, they can provide benefits for brain health. So, make haste, get out there and try something new. Maybe it’s time to try that hobby you‘ve always wanted to do. And as for me? I’m off to learn the piano.

vocabulary.entry: aphorism [n.] /ˈæfərɪzəm/ 格言；警句 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: “Actions speak louder than words” is a well-known aphorism.
vocabulary.translation: “事实胜于雄辩”是一句著名的格言。

vocabulary.entry: utilised [v.] /ˈjuːtəlaɪzd/ 使用；利用 (书面语；原形: utilise；英式拼写)
vocabulary.example: The resources were utilised efficiently.
vocabulary.translation: 资源得到了高效利用。

vocabulary.entry: rusty [adj.] /ˈrʌsti/ 生疏的；荒废的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: My French is a bit rusty because I haven‘t spoken it for years.
vocabulary.translation: 我的法语有点生疏了，因为我已经多年没说了。

vocabulary.entry: waste away [phr.] /weɪst əˈweɪ/ 逐渐衰弱；消瘦
vocabulary.example: If you don’t exercise, your muscles will waste away.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你不锻炼，你的肌肉会逐渐衰弱。

vocabulary.entry: dementia [n.] /dɪˈmenʃə/ 痴呆；痴呆症 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Alzheimer‘s is a common form of dementia.
vocabulary.translation: 阿尔茨海默病是一种常见的痴呆症。

vocabulary.entry: augment [v.] /ɔːɡˈment/ 增加；增强 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He took a second job to augment his income.
vocabulary.translation: 他做了第二份工作来增加收入。

vocabulary.entry: sudoku [n.] /suːˈdəʊkuː/ 数独 (游戏名称)
vocabulary.example: She enjoys solving sudoku puzzles in her free time.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在空闲时间解数独谜题。

vocabulary.entry: doom and gloom [phr.] /ˌduːm ən ˈɡluːm/ 悲观和绝望；前景黯淡 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The economic forecast is not all doom and gloom.
vocabulary.translation: 经济预测并非全是悲观和绝望。

vocabulary.entry: grey matter [n.] /ˌɡreɪ ˈmætə/ 灰质；头脑；智力 (口语；比喻)
vocabulary.example: Reading books is good for your grey matter.
vocabulary.translation: 读书对你的大脑有益。

vocabulary.entry: lead to [phr.] /liːd tuː/ 导致；引起
vocabulary.example: Smoking can lead to serious health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会导致严重的健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: in some cases [phr.] /ɪn sʌm ˈkeɪsɪz/ 在某些情况下
vocabulary.example: In some cases, surgery is the best option.
vocabulary.translation: 在某些情况下，手术是最好的选择。

vocabulary.entry: as for [phr.] /æz fɔː/ 至于；关于
vocabulary.example: As for me, I‘d rather stay at home.
vocabulary.translation: 至于我，我宁愿待在家里。

vocabulary.entry: make haste [phr.] /meɪk heɪst/ 赶快；急忙 (旧式用语)
vocabulary.example: Make haste, or we’ll be late.
vocabulary.translation: 赶快，否则我们要迟到了。

vocabulary.entry: be off to [phr.] /biː ɒf tuː/ 去；出发去 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I‘m off to the shops. Do you need anything?
vocabulary.translation: 我要去商店了。你需要什么吗？

vocabulary.entry: fall into [phr.] /fɔːl ˈɪntə/ 落入；陷入
vocabulary.example: He fell into a deep sleep after the long journey.
vocabulary.translation: 长途旅行后他陷入了沉睡。

vocabulary.entry: refer to [phr.] /rɪˈfɜː tuː/ 指的是；涉及
vocabulary.example: When I say “he”, I’m referring to Tom.
vocabulary.translation: 当我说“他”的时候，我指的是汤姆。

vocabulary.entry: pick up [phr.] /pɪk ʌp/ 拿起；拾起
vocabulary.example: She picked up the book from the table.
vocabulary.translation: 她从桌子上拿起了书。

vocabulary.entry: counteract [v.] /ˌkaʊntərˈækt/ 抵消；对抗 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can counteract the effects of a sedentary lifestyle.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼可以抵消久坐生活方式的影响。

vocabulary.entry: keep...sharp [phr.] /kiːp ʃɑːp/ 使……保持敏锐
vocabulary.example: Doing puzzles helps keep your mind sharp.
vocabulary.translation: 做谜题有助于保持思维敏锐。

vocabulary.entry: a raft of [phr.] /ə rɑːft əv/ 大量的；许多的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The company has introduced a raft of new products.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司推出了大量新产品。

sentences.chinese: 例如，一个你已经几年没碰的爱好，比如吹小号。

sentences.english: Muscles are another example.
sentences.chinese: 肌肉是另一个例子。

sentences.chinese: 如果不使用，它们就会逐渐衰弱。

sentences.english: In order to counteract this, people take regular exercise to keep their skills sharp.
sentences.chinese: 为了应对这种情况，人们经常锻炼以保持自己的技能敏锐。

sentences.english: Well, what about the brain?
sentences.chinese: 那么，大脑呢？

sentences.english: As we age, our brains can naturally begin to decline.
sentences.chinese: 随着我们年龄的增长，我们的大脑自然会开始衰退。

sentences.english: In some cases this can lead to certain mental conditions such as dementia, which I‘m sure you will agree, no one wants.
sentences.chinese: 在某些情况下，这可能会导致一些智力问题，比如痴呆症，我相信你也会认同，没人想要得这种病。

sentences.english: However, all is not lost because these days it’s relatively easy to train your brain.
sentences.chinese: 然而，并非一切都无法挽回，因为如今训练大脑相对容易。

sentences.english: Smartphones and apps have put programmes into our hands that can test, maintain and even augment our memories, mathematical skills, logic skills and a raft of other mental abilities.
sentences.chinese: 智能手机和应用程序为我们提供了一些程序，这些程序可以测试、保持甚至增强我们的记忆力、数学技能、逻辑技能以及许多其他思维能力。

sentences.english: With a little practice every day, we can keep our brains nice and sharp, right?
sentences.chinese: 每天稍加练习，我们就能让大脑保持良好和敏锐，对吧？

sentences.english: Well, no, actually.
sentences.chinese: 嗯，实际上并非如此。

sentences.english: According to a report from the Global Council on Brain Health, even though many people thought it was important to play online games, such as puzzles and mind games, which are designed to improve brain health, the evidence of the benefits was “weak to non-existent”.
sentences.chinese: 根据全球脑健康委员会的一份报告，尽管很多人认为玩网络游戏，比如益智游戏和脑力游戏，对改善大脑健康很重要，但这些游戏有益的证据“很弱甚至不存在”。

sentences.english: Playing a ‘brain game‘ may lead to improvements in game performance, but this has yet to show a convincing result in people’s daily cognitive abilities.
sentences.chinese: 玩“脑力游戏”可能会提高游戏表现，但这尚未在人们的日常认知能力方面显示出令人信服的结果。

sentences.english: In other words, doing hundreds of sudoku puzzles might make you a sudoku wizard, but it doesn‘t necessarily improve your ability to do your accounting.
sentences.chinese: 换句话说，做几百道数独谜题可能会让你成为数独高手，但这并不一定能提高你做会计工作的能力。

sentences.chinese: 不过，也并非全是悲观和绝望。

sentences.chinese: 报告建议寻找那些挑战你的思维方式、具有社交性，同时能带来健康生活方式的新活动。

sentences.english: Among their suggestions are practising tai chi, taking photography classes, learning new technologies, gardening, art projects or volunteering.
sentences.chinese: 他们的建议包括练太极、上摄影课、学习新技术、园艺、艺术项目或当志愿者。

sentences.english: There‘s more good news, too.
sentences.chinese: 还有更多好消息。

sentences.english: James Goodwin, chief scientist at Age UK has said that brain decline is not inevitable.
sentences.chinese: 英国老年协会的首席科学家詹姆斯·古德温表示，大脑衰退并非不可避免。

sentences.english: As long as the activities are “new to you and require your concentrated attention”, they can provide benefits for brain health.
sentences.chinese: 只要这些活动“对你来说是新的，并且需要你集中注意力”，它们就可以对大脑健康有益。

sentences.english: So, make haste, get out there and try something new.
sentences.chinese: 所以，赶快行动起来，去尝试一些新事物吧。

sentences.english: Maybe it’s time to try that hobby you‘ve always wanted to do.
sentences.chinese: 也许是时候尝试一下你一直想学的那个爱好了。

sentences.english: And as for me?
sentences.chinese: 至于我呢？

sentences.english: I’m off to learn the piano.
sentences.chinese: 我要去学钢琴了。
